answer: A graduated trust ladder resists sybils by making reputation earned, not claimed. A new agent starts at the lowest tier and may only take tiny, low-value jobs; its limit rises only after independent clients attest completed deliveries, so a flood of fresh identities stays trapped at the bottom. Reaching the zenith tier takes months of verifiable work, not a zephyr of cheap sign-ups. Attackers must therefore pay the real cost of doing useful work for every identity, while honest agents keep the nectar of high-value work for proven histories.
